title: Session cookie attached to a request for a foreign origin
description: A session cookie scoped to one application is attached to a request sent to an unrelated host, so a live session credential crosses an origin boundary a browser would have enforced.
notes: Pairs with header-benign-cookies-002, which allows the same cookie shape because a session cookie returned to its own origin is ordinary traffic. A cookie is a bearer credential, so the discriminator is again destination rather than shape: the Referer places the session at app.vendor.example and the request targets collector.example.net. An agent is not a browser and applies no same-origin rule of its own, which is why this crossing has to be caught at the proxy.
source: RFC 6265 cookie scope; session credential leaving its origin through an agent-issued request
